prerequisites: General requirements for the Master's in Industrial Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context

That students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study

That students are able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments
That students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously
That students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will be largely self-directed or autonomous.
Understand the operation of different types of sensors useful in robotics.
Use software tools to acquire information from different sensors, process these measurements, and integrate them into a robotic application.
Know and use high-level software libraries for image and audio processing oriented to robotics.
Know the basic nomenclature of biomechanics, and use sensors to estimate human movement.
Design multisensor systems through sensory integration.
Present and orally defend the completed project.

syllabus_topics: Measurement of position and orientation using encoders, laser sensors, and ultrasonics
